pages.text: "Gulp, gulp! Quick, a drink!" Tumba the warthog ran from digging on the red dirt path. Muddy hooves splashed into the waterhole. "Tumba, what about your hooves?" Moya asked. Tumba pretended not to hear.
"Washing takes too long! I want to drink and dig again!" Tumba stamped in the water. Dirt slipped from their hooves, turning it yellow and muddy. Gulp, gulp went Tumba.
Soon Tumba's tummy rumbled and ached. "Oh, my tummy..." They lowered their snout to it, eyes watering. Moya called toward the acacia shade. "Mom! Tumba's tummy hurts!"
Mom examined Tumba's hooves. "All that dirt mixed into the water, then you swallowed it." Tumba looked up. "What do I do?" "Come with me to the shallows."
They stood side by side. "Wash your hooves, then drink! There are three steps. One, dip your hooves in shallow water!" Tumba splashed their front hooves in. Dirt loosened and drifted away.
"Two, rub your hooves on a flat stone underwater!" Tumba rubbed and rubbed. Clumps of dirt fell away. "My hooves are turning black!" Moya joined in happily.
"Three, dip and rinse your snout, too!" Tumba dipped their snout, and the dirt washed off. "One, two, three—wash your hooves, then drink! Bye, dirt!" Black hooves gleamed.
At the drinking spot, Tumba gulped clear, cool water. After a good rest, their aching tummy gradually felt better. "The water's so clear when I wash first!" Their tail popped up.
The next day, Tumba called, "Wait! Hooves first!" One, dip in the shallows. Two, rub on a flat stone. Three, rinse the snout! Now Tumba could do it all alone.

Mom nuzzled Tumba's forehead. "Our hoof-washing champion!" Washing first kept the water clear and tummies happy. "Wash your hooves, then drink!" Tumba and Moya gulped water that tasted twice as refreshing.
